rules.title: Newark Rent Control Ordinance - Annual Rent Increase Limit
rules.requirement: Landlords in Newark may not raise rent at lease renewal or periodic tenancy termination by more than the percentage change in the Consumer Price Index over a specified period, and in no case may the increase exceed 4% in any 12-month period.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all multiple dwellings as defined in the ordinance (buildings containing one or more apartments rented or offered for rent), unless exempt under the chapter's exemption list.
rules.exemptions: Public housing; motel/hotel space rented day-to-day to transients; commercial space; newly constructed multiple dwellings and vacant dwellings (per §§19:2-18.1 and 19:2-18.2); units rehabilitated under Federal/State Rental Rehabilitation Programs receiving Section 8 subsidies (exempt only during subsidy tenure); units subject to a governmental agency rent-regulation contract that supersedes city authority.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the dwelling is a newly constructed multiple dwelling or vacant dwelling exempt under §§19:2-18.1/19:2-18.2, or is subject to a Section 8/Rental Rehabilitation subsidy or a government rent-regulation contract

rules.conflict_note: The ordinance has been amended multiple times (most recently referenced 05-20-2026 amendment to definitions section and 09-18-2024 amendment to the rent increase section); exact current effective date of the 4% cap provision is not stated in this chunk.
